data.long_meaning: The name Huriyyah in Arabic means freedom, liberty, and release from bondage. It is a powerful name that resonates with the spirit of independence and self-determination. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that Allah (SWT) grants us the freedom to choose our own path in life, and Huriyyah is a reminder of this fundamental truth.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the spiritual freedom and liberation from the shackles of worldly desires and attachments, allowing one to focus on their journey towards Allah (SWT).
data.etymology: Huriyyah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Freedom, Liberty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Huriyyah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Huriyyah holds significant cultural importance in the Islamic world, particularly in the context of struggle for freedom and independence. This name was given to many children during times of political upheaval and revolution, as a symbol of hope and inspiration for a future of liberty and self-governance. In modern times, it is still used as a powerful name for those who strive for personal and collective freedom, reflecting the enduring spirit of the Islamic faith.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Huriyyah represents the ultimate gift of Allah (SWT) – the freedom to choose our own path in life, free from the shackles of sin and ignorance. It is a reminder that every individual has the power to break free from the chains of their own limitations and live a life of purpose and meaning. The name Huriyyah also carries the promise of the eternal freedom that awaits us in the hereafter, a place where we will be free from all suffering and pain, and reunited with our loved ones. Overall, the name Huriyyah is a powerful symbol of the transformative power of the Islamic faith, inspiring us to strive for personal and collective freedom, both in this world and the next.
